Question: What harmful effect can a single chest X-ray have on the fetus of a one-month-old pregnancy?
Answer: Thanks for A 2A In nut shell single inadvertent x Ray chest in pregnancy is not likely to cause harm to the fetus in the womb. Today’s X Ray machines deliver focussed dose to the organ and create inages. Theorotically even if one considers chance of scattered beam … it would give miniscule dose.. way too low for harming the baby. Here are few things that every one should remember: 1 X Ray and CT scan use ionising rays and these ray my have potential to cause damage to the fetus. It is obvious that the damage is dose dependent. 2 Sonography and MRI DONOT use ionising rays and have no side effects on the baby. 3 All women who are pregnant or are doubtfully / potentially pregnant MUST inform the radiographer before going for X Ray or CT 4 Using lead apron as a barrier can significantly reduce the exposure of x rays to the abdomen and fetus. What factors decide the magnitude of fetal harm? 1 How many X rays were done? 2 Which part of the body was exposed? 3 What was the gestation / months of pregnancy? Here I attach 2 tables. The first one shows effects of radiation and the other one shows the amount of radiation given by various X ray tests. Careful study of the above prove the point that inadvertent single X Ray chest exposure won't be a cause of a concern and most of the doctors will not advice termination of pregnancy for the same. Detailed scientific report from American College of Obstetricians and gynaecologist s is quoted here. https://m.acog.org/Clinical-Guidance-and-Publications/Committee-Opinions/Committee-on-Obstetric-Practice/Guidelines-for-Diagnostic-Imaging-During-Pregnancy-and-Lactation?IsMobileSet=true

Question: Why doesn’t menstrual blood clot?
Answer: When the lining of the uterus is shed out it is called menstruation. The lining cells called endometrium also secrete anti coagulants which prevents the menstrual blood from clotting. If clots are appearing in the menstruation that is a sign of probably heavy bleeding.

Question: What are the significances of fundal height in pregnancy and during postpartum?
Answer: The Fundal height means the top of the uterus. The Fundal height grows as pregnancy grows. And it reduces after delivery. The size of the uterus is bigger when baby is big, water inside is more or if it is twins. Fundal height is less if baby is small or there is less of water. Of course worngly given dates by the patient can also be a factor. We gynaecologists check the Fundal height every time to make a rough assessment of how baby in the womb is growing.
